s1.syndrome_frame: Acute lower abdominal pain and urinary symptoms with a palpable mass
salient_findings: Palpable mass extending from the bladder dome to the posterior surface of the umbilicus
key_facts: 2-day history of burning on urination
Urinary frequency and nocturia
Constant 5/10 suprapubic pain
Denies fever, nausea, vomiting, and changes in bowel movements
Last menstrual period was one week earlier
Lower abdominal tenderness, most pronounced in the para-umbilical area
Urinalysis with 10–25 WBCs per high-power field, moderate bacteria, moderate mucus, moderate yeast, and positive nitrites
Negative serum β-hCG, normal CBC and BMP
Cervical NAAT was negative for Neisseria gonorrhoeae and Chlamydia trachomatis
Contrast-enhanced CT scan showed a 4.0 × 3.3 × 6.8 cm multiloculated, enhancing hypodense and isodense mass
Mass extends superiorly from the dome of the bladder to the posterior surface of the umbilicus
Surrounding acute inflammatory stranding and minimal fluid
Possible invasion into the bladder dome

shortlist.label: Urachal cyst
shortlist.why_kept: CT scan showed a multiloculated mass extending from the bladder dome to the posterior surface of the umbilicus, consistent with a urachal cyst

shortlist.label: Bladder cancer
shortlist.why_kept: Mass effect on the bladder dome and possible invasion, raising concern for a malignant process such as bladder cancer

shortlist.label: Urachal sinus
shortlist.why_kept: Similar presentation to urachal cyst, with the mass located near the bladder dome and umbilicus, suggesting a possible urachal sinus

shortlist.label: Sarcoma botryoides
shortlist.why_kept: Imaging findings of a multiloculated mass with possible invasion into the bladder dome, which could be consistent with a rare tumor like sarcoma botryoides

shortlist.label: Rhabdomyosarcoma
shortlist.why_kept: Aggressive features on imaging, such as the large size of the mass and surrounding inflammatory stranding, which could suggest a malignant tumor like rhabdomyosarcoma

raw.rationale: The patient's symptoms and imaging findings, including a multiloculated mass extending from the bladder dome to the posterior surface of the umbilicus, are consistent with a urachal cyst, which is a congenital anomaly that can present with urinary symptoms and a midline abdominal mass.

rejected.label: Bladder cancer
rejected.why: Less likely given the patient's age and lack of other risk factors

rejected.label: Urachal sinus
rejected.why: Typically presents with a fistulous tract and recurrent infections

rejected.label: Sarcoma botryoides
rejected.why: Typically occurs in infants and young children

rejected.label: Rhabdomyosarcoma
rejected.why: Typically presents with a rapidly growing mass and systemic symptoms
